newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin threatens Belarus accord over tv crew row.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin threatens Belarus accord over tv crew row.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin was quoted by Interfax news agency on Wednesday as threatening to revise a union charter with Belarus in a row over the detention of a Russian television crew.

Yeltsin said he was "surprised and indignant" over the arrest by Belarussian authorities of a Russian Public Television (ORT) team on Saturday for what they said was illegally filming and crossing the Belarus-Lithuania border.

Interfax quoted Yeltsin as telling reporters at the Volzhsky Utyos holiday residence in central Russia to convey his words to Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko: "I am indignant over your actions. I want you to explain what is happening."
Yeltsin said he hoped the incident could be settled, but if it was not, then: "Let us reconsider the charter and the agreements which we have signed". He added: "We do not touch Belarus journalists."
One of the points in the union charter signed in May by Yeltsin and Lukashenko provided for the protection of press freedoms.

Lukashenko, seen by liberals in Moscow and in the West as increasingly authoritarian, defended the action against the ORT journalists on Monday and accused the Russian media of waging an information war against him.
